newsitem.title: KUWAIT: Director of Kuwait's KIA keeps post for four years.
newsitem.headline: Director of Kuwait's KIA keeps post for four years.

text.p: Kuwait Investment Authority (KIA) managing director Ali al-Badr will run the Gulf Arab state's investment arm's $40 billion global portfolio for another four-year term, a KIA spokesman said on Tuesday.
Badr's term was renewed on Monday during a board meeting headed by Finance Minister Nasser al-Rodhan, KIA's Khaled al-Tarah told Reuters.
Sticking to official policy, Badr declined to disclose in a Reuters interview in April the size of KIA's foreign portfolio but economists said it was currently worth around $40 billion.
KIA, once a key global investor, saw the nestegg shrink to around $30 billion from over $100 billion after paying for the 1991 Gulf War against Iraq, reconstruction and financing budget deficits.

KIA is also in charge of the first phase of the government's privatisation plan which has earned the state some $2.4 billion since 1994. KIA plans to shed further government shares in local firms worth more than $3 billion by the end of 1998.

KIA's board is made up of four ex-officio members -- the ministers of oil and finance, the Central Bank governor and the undersecretary for the ministry of finance -- and five independent members, including Badr.
